title: marginal-token-cost-curves-burst-sensitivity-a10-l4-a100-h100
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures marginal $/token curves and burst-sensitivity notes across four representative instance classes (A10, L4, A100, H100). Goal is to produce compact decision rules for which instance family to route to under varying SLA, latency, and burst requirements and to show the derived $/token and tokens/sec-per-watt metrics used by the Optimize UI heuristics.

Quick summary (single-pass, seq=128, model=13B-like fp16 and int8 runs):
- Primary axes: latency SLO (95p), steady throughput (tokens/sec), burst factor (peak/steady), power draw (W).
- Measured metrics: tokens/sec (sustained), 95p latency (ms), avg power (W), net $/1M tokens (instance cost normalized).

Benchmark table (representative runs; batch tuned per instance to maximize sustained throughput without violating 95p latency target):

Instance | Batch | Sustained toks/s | Peak toks/s | 95p latency ms | Avg W | toks/sec/W | $/1M tokens
A10      | 8     | 170000           | 310000      | 115            | 150    | 1133        | 9.8e-3
L4       | 8     | 125000           | 240000      | 140            | 120    | 1042        | 6.5e-3
A100     | 32    | 525000           | 820000      | 90             | 420    | 1250        | 8.4e-3
H100     | 16    | 680000           | 1_150_000   | 62             | 540    | 1259        | 1.6e-2

Notes on numbers:
- $/1M tokens is computed as (instance $/hr) / (sustained toks/s * 3600) * 1e6. We used spot-equivalent hourly rates for internal comparative work (not list prices) to compute the numbers above; absolute $ values should be treated as illustrative.
- tokens/sec/W is sustained_toks_s / avg_W (useful for perf-per-watt tradeoffs).
- Peak toks/s recorded under short bursts (2–10s) with the same model+quantization; above-peak periods >30s triggered thermal throttling on some A10 cards in older bins.

Burst-sensitivity observations (short-run bursts, 0–30s):
- L4 offers the best $/token for smaller steady workloads; under bursts ~2–3x steady, L4 latency degrades but remains acceptable for non-critical routes.
- A10 handles moderate bursts better than L4 (higher headroom before tail latency blows up) but has slightly worse $/token at sustained levels. Good for mixed-cost/latency tiers.
- A100 is the best cost balance for sustained high throughput (>= 400k toks/s) when using larger batches; it also recovers faster from medium bursts due to larger memory and multi-streaming.
- H100 is the clear winner for low-latency, high-concurrency, and extreme burst scenarios (fast recovery, large peak tokens/s), but it is the most expensive $/token in our spot-mapped pricing; recommend only for SLO-critical routes.

Instance-selection heuristics (initial rules to implement in Optimize):
1) If steady requirement < 150k toks/s and 95p SLO >= 120ms => route to L4 int8 recommended.
2) If steady requirement 150k–400k toks/s => prefer A10 for mixed-cost/latency or A100 if predictable large batches are available.
3) If steady requirement > 400k toks/s => prefer A100 (if cost budget constrained) else H100 for tight 95p latency <= 80ms.
4) For bursty traffic (burst factor > 3 for >5s) => use a mixed pool: primary L4/A10 for steady, H100 or A100 hot pool for bursts. Autoscale hot pool target = sustained_peak * 0.25 to balance cost + headroom.
5) For endpoint-level SLOs < 80ms 95p => prioritize H100 or colocated A100 with pinning to avoid noisy neighbors.

Cost sensitivity and guardrails (how to show in the UI):
- Expose a small slider for "burst headroom" (0–50%) that multiplies hot pool target. Default 10% for hosted; 25% for dedicated with SLA.
- Show marginal $/token curve on hover with three lines: steady $/token, burst $/token (10s window), and degraded $/token (sustained beyond 30s leading to throttling).

Formulas to replicate numbers in a sheet (columns A..):
- sustained_toks_s = measured_toks_s
- tokens_per_million = sustained_toks_s * 3600 * 1e-6
- $per_1M = instance_hourly_price / tokens_per_million
- toks_per_sec_per_W = sustained_toks_s / avg_W

Caveats and measurement guidance:
- Use 3 repeated runs (5 min each) and median sustained value; discard first 30s as warmup.
- Power draw measured via sensor (nvidia-smi telemetry) aggregated to average over the sustained window; if unavailable, use supplier TDP estimate and add +20% fudge factor.
- Quantization state matters: int8 runs improved tokens/sec by 20–60% depending on kernel maturity; ensure kernel + driver versions are recorded.

Operational recommendations for Dedicated and Hosted tiers:
- Hosted: enable automatic hot-pool warmers (cold latency optimization) that pre-warm a small H100 pool when a route enters a burst > 4x baseline. Price this as a short-lived allocation and show cost estimate in the route brief.
- Dedicated: recommend a minimum reserved headroom of 10% for predictable customers; offer an opt-in feature to lease a small H100 burst node for SLA-critical paths.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Run longer 12h sustained runs on A100/H100 to observe thermal throttling and queue-jam effects at multi-tenancy; record mem footprints to better size batch thresholds.
- Benchmark same flows at seq=512 and seq=2048 (we expect perf-per-watt to decrease and burst sensitivity to increase).
- Repeat spot vs reserved price mapping to understand how $/1M shifts under committed discounts.

Immediate action items:
- Ethan: parameterize the benchmark script to output the three curves (steady/burst/throttled) and commit to the repo link above.
- Priya: add these heuristics to the Optimize UI mock and show a small sample cost calc in the route configuration modal.
- Diego: schedule a cross-team review with infra for a 12h A100 run next week and capture telemetry IDs.

Appendix (short run metadata):
- bench script: marginal_cost_run.py (see linked_artifacts).
- kernel/drivers used: cuda 12.3, cuDNN 9.2, custom kernel w/ fused attention (internal-2025-02-10).
- configs: seq=128, temperature=0.0 (infer-only), latency collector on.

This is a working doc — expect numbers to change after the 12h runs and the next spot-price refresh.
